about: Patterns in Insights (no AI; UX 2026-11-04). From the person's own check-ins: mood on the SAME check-in, split by one factor. Window: a fixed 90 days, today − 89 … today inclusive (the profile's local dates), on every Insights tab; rows after today are ignored. Gate: fewer than minCheckIns check-ins in the window (any row with a mood, with or without a factor) → every pattern not_enough. Averages are sum / count of the integer moods (no running mean), then rounded. Pairs, in this fixed order (never sorted): sleep (a: sleep_hours ≥ sleepHoursAtLeast; b: below), movement (a: exercise_minutes > 0; b: = 0), stress (a: stressLow; b: stressHigh). A null factor is left out, never a group; stress 3 is left out; sleep_hours may arrive as a string (read it as a number). Each side needs ≥ minPerSide days, else not_enough (a, b, diff null; the UI hides it). a.mood and b.mood: the side's average mood rounded to 1 decimal, halves away from zero, −0 → 0. diff = the same rounding of (a.mood − b.mood), from the ROUNDED averages. |diff| ≥ sameBelow → shown; below → same (both numbers shown, "about the same"). The UI shows one none line when no pattern is shown or same. "copy" is UX's English text (approved 2026-11-04): the app ARB and the web messages use it word for word; {a} and {b} are the one-decimal moods.

copy.title: Patterns in your check-ins
copy.subtitle: In the last 3 months
copy.sleepShown: On days after 7 or more hours of sleep, your mood averaged {a} of 5. After less sleep, {b}.
copy.sleepSame: After 7 or more hours of sleep and after less, your mood was about the same ({a} and {b} of 5).
copy.movementShown: On days you moved, your mood averaged {a} of 5. On days you didn't, {b}.
copy.movementSame: On days you moved and days you didn't, your mood was about the same ({a} and {b} of 5).
copy.stressShown: On low-stress days, your mood averaged {a} of 5. On high-stress days, {b}.
copy.stressSame: On low- and high-stress days, your mood was about the same ({a} and {b} of 5).
copy.footnote: These are your own check-ins side by side. They may show what tends to go together, not what causes what.
copy.none: Patterns show up here once you have more check-ins with sleep, movement or stress.

cases.name: all three shown: 10 good days, 10 harder days
gate: 13 check-ins in the window, nothing shows
per side: exactly 5 is enough, 4 is not
sleep exactly 7 counts as 7+; 6.5 is less; a string "7" is 7
movement: 0 is "none", null is left out
stress 3 is left out (only 3s: not enough)
stress 3 left out between low and high
a gap of exactly 0.5 is shown (3.8 vs 3.3, not 0.4999…)
a gap of 0.4 is "same", with both numbers
rounding: halves go away from zero (3.25 → 3.3, 3.75 → 3.8)
real doubles: 69/20 = 3.45 → 3.5 and 67/20 = 3.35 → 3.4 (the same IEEE steps on both sides)
a negative gap is shown the same way (A lower than B)
rows 90+ days ago or after today are ignored (and not counted for the gate)
nothing but moods: every pattern not enough (the none line)
